speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what preventive and oversight measures are in place to ensure telehealth providers meet patient care standards consistently; and (b) whether additional regulatory frameworks will be developed to monitor the quality and duration of teleconsultations to safeguard patient outcomes.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the Ministry's announcement on 24 October 2024 to revoke a medical clinic's licence (a) how may the Ministry assure the public that teleconsultation services provided by medical clinics meet the appropriate standards; and (b) whether the Ministry has been receiving feedback on potentially errant medical clinics.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the case of healthcare, medical practitioners themselves also need to adhere to the ethical and professional standards set out in the Singapore Medical Council's (SMC's) Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (ECEG).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Under the guidelines, they must obtain sufficient information from their patients, conduct appropriate clinical assessment and ensure that any provision of medical care, prescription of medicines and issuance of medical certificates (MCs) are justified on proper medical grounds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In other words, the regulation of telemedicine is not different from regulation of all other economic activities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We set standards, we require licensing, we conduct periodic audits for each clinic, investigate complaints and take offenders to task.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Such regulatory frameworks cannot eradicate offenders – that is not possible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But instead, it ensures that when practices have gone astray, especially with the advent of new technology and business models, they can be corrected promptly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is exactly what happened with the MaNaDr case.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I do believe quality assurance mechanisms are important.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In that regard, how does the Ministry currently assess the quality of telehealth consultations?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Are there metrics or periodic audits in place to monitor performance?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And are these criteria laid out specifically to all these telemedicine providers?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The other question I have, Sir, is really on patient feedback.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I have had students who used telemedicine as the form of them getting a medical certificate (MC) in school; and sometimes, I do hear they have complaints and feedback.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Could the Minister share if there are specific feedback mechanisms or complaint channels in place for telehealth services and how patients' concerns are addressed within this framework?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member asked if there are standards, if there are audits and if we receive complaints and feedback.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would say, in terms of standards and audits, all the clinics know – we have some doctors in the House – you know the standards, you know we audit you.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And if, despite knowing all these, you still fall foul of the regulations and the SMC's Ethical Guidelines, then, you are in trouble, because we will catch you.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And even if we do not catch you, people will complain – which is the case here, people complained about MaNaDr, that the turnaround was too fast and MCs are issued; employers are suffering, particularly, because their employees are not coming to work, applying for MCs, sometimes, while they are overseas through telemedicine.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Be mindful that while the offence went on for awhile, it was not a long while.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We investigated, took action and corrected the situation.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first is, for the purposes of the audit, whether the Ministry has been conducting any mystery shopping consultations?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Otherwise, is this something that it will consider doing amongst other measures for auditing purposes?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am not entirely familiar with the operational aspects of enforcement, but I think we take the attitude that if mystery shopping is required, we will do so, bearing in mind the public are our eyes and ears.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When they see something is wrong, they will usually whistle-blow and let us know.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And when you see a pattern of complaints, we will take action quite promptly, which is what happened in this case.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Whether there needs to be a review, I do not think so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While telemedicine is due to new technology, post-COVID-19, and it is a new business model, the principles and standards and requirements lay out – whether under HCSA or SMC's Guidelines – I think they are still applicable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For that matter, HCSA was just recently enacted, taking into account technology and taking into account a post-COVID-19, ageing population healthcare system, where technology is being used.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, if you want an MC from the polyclinics, you would still have to turn up in person.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many of my Yio Chu Kang residents are seniors and many of them have mobility issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Hence, telehealth services would be useful for them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I hope this incident will not hinder the push for telehealth services, which will benefit many residents on the ground.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My question is, given this incident, can the Ministry share how we can continue to promote telehealth services amongst the seniors and continue to build trust and confidence in this mode of service delivery?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think when we have new technology, we have an opportunity to make service better, to serve patients and residents better.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But just like all new technology, all new business models, someone will try to abuse it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And then, questions will be raised: is the Ministry stepping up audit, enforcement, regulation, doing a clamp-down?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is always a temptation to do so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you do so, you stop being able to seize the opportunities that new technology can present you.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is why I want to be quite honest with Members.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the current requirements and standards are valid and our enforcement has been effective.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, something gone wrong, we corrected it straight away.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And what Mr Yip Hon Weng mentioned, I think, can come true.
